candidates.title: Next Token or Vector? Learning How Far to Decode
candidates.abstract: Standard autoregressive decoding advances one token at a time, even when several upcoming tokens can be predicted together. We propose CADENCE (Context-Adaptive DEcoding), a generation method that learns both what to draft and how far to draft. Gaussian prediction heads represent future spans as continuous latent vectors, and a shared decoder converts the selected vector into token predictions in parallel. A learned router selects the prediction length from the model's own hidden states and predicted Gaussian parameters, adapting generation granularity to the current context with single-token generation as a fallback. The backbone verifies each proposed continuation and retains the prefix that matches its greedy predictions. Experiments with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on Alpaca, GSM8K, and HumanEval show that router-selected positions yield higher draft acceptance than applying the corresponding prediction length everywhere. CADENCE achieves up to 1.3x higher generation throughput than standard greedy decoding.
candidates.reason: 未来区間をガウス潜在ベクトルで下書きし検証器が貪欲予測と一致する接頭辞を保持するCADENCEにより、文脈適応的に下書き長を選んで貪欲デコード比で最大1.3倍の生成スループットを得ており、投機的デコード機構への直接貢献である。

candidates.title: Understanding GPU Megakernels: Why Residency Can Mislead
candidates.abstract: Megakernels let one persistent GPU program prepare dependent operators early and execute ready tasks together. We study the benefits and costs of these capabilities by reconstructing two LLM megakernels, ThunderKittens (TK) and VDCores, as separate kernels on H100 using their original operator code. Our results show that CTA residency can misrepresent opportunities for useful overlap in both directions. By overlapping startup and operand loading with programmatic dependent launch (PDL), the reconstructions reduce decode-step latency by 5.7% in TK and achieve comparable performance in VDCores when both executions enforce the required memory ordering. Under whole-operator dependencies, TK's persistent execution still gains more from prefetch, but runtime and completion-signal ordering costs outweigh this advantage. Both startup overlap and prefetch depend on resource availability. Persistent CTAs can reuse storage before retiring, whereas separate successors must acquire their full CTA footprints before initializing or loading operands. This admission constraint in both reconstructions motivates finer resource sharing across kernels. Beyond early preparation, joint execution requires ready work and spare capacity in the bottleneck resource. Reserving SMs for communication can add GEMM waves that erase overlap gains, while filling idle SMs offers little benefit once memory bandwidth is saturated. These findings clarify benefits and costs of megakernels and motivate GPU support for earlier resource reuse across kernels.
candidates.reason: H100上でThunderKittensとVDCoresのメガカーネルを独立カーネルへ再構成し、CTA常駐率が重なり機会を誤らせること、PDLによる起動・ロード重なりでデコードステップ遅延を5.7%削減できることを示すGPUカーネル実行の計測研究で、推論カーネル設計への直接貢献である。

candidates.title: LiquidCP: Decoupling Attention Tasks from Communication and Kernel Boundaries in Context Parallelism
candidates.abstract: Context parallelism (CP) partitions long sequences across GPUs for LLM training and inference. For variable-length training and full prefill, attention-balanced placement can leave token loads uneven, while ring execution repeats overhead at each computation and communication step. In stage-serialized decode CP (DCP), long-running tasks delay dependent work and leave substantial GPU hardware idle. We propose LiquidCP, which unifies training and inference through a common model of Transfer, Compute, and Reduction tasks with tile-level dependencies, decoupling attention tasks from communication and kernel boundaries. For training and full prefill, MegaRing incorporates BuddyRing placement to balance attention and token loads, and coalesces ready KV regions during forward attention to amortize overhead. For decoding and mixed batches, MegaDCP selects history-KV splits by jointly modeling the completion of attention and its dependent reductions. A shared persistent GPU-resident engine executes both designs. Compared with the fastest baseline per configuration on eight H100 GPUs, MegaRing achieves geometric-mean core-attention speedups of $1.23\times$ forward and $1.18\times$ backward, and accelerates a Transformer layer by $1.08$--$1.16\times$. MegaDCP achieves geometric-mean core-attention speedups of $1.20\times$ for decode-only and $1.35\times$ for mixed batches. In vLLM serving with KV prefix cache, it achieves an average time-to-first-token speedup of $1.22\times$.
candidates.reason: 文脈並列化をTransfer・Compute・Reductionタスクへ分解しカーネル境界から注意タスクを切り離すLiquidCPで、学習・プリフィルとデコード混在バッチ双方のGPUアイドルを減らす永続エンジンを実装しており、分散推論実行方式への直接貢献である。

candidates.title: Recursive Sparse Attention: Million-Token Length Extrapolation at Logarithmic Cost
candidates.abstract: At context lengths of about 1M tokens, dense attention is costly in prefill and decoding, and training typically relies on long documents, which become scarcer as the target length increases. Most sparse attention methods score all preceding blocks or tokens, so their selection cost per query is $O(L)$ at context length $L$; hierarchical selection reduces it to $O(\log L)$, but prior trainable hierarchical methods report accuracy only within their training length. We propose RecSA (Recursive Sparse Attention), which builds a tree over the KV cache in which each node summarizes its subtree with one key and one mean-pooled value. The keys come from one pooler per layer, shared by all levels and distilled from dense attention. Each level above the tokens selects at most $k$ candidates, so each query has $O(\log L)$ selection cost and reads $O(\log L)$ entries; the summaries of unselected candidates share one softmax with the exact tokens. Each entry's RoPE position is its index among the candidates of its level, so at any length every relative distance stays within the range seen during training. Initialized from Qwen3-4B and trained on 0.62B tokens at the original model's 32K training length, RecSA outperforms all baselines on RULER at every length from 131K to 2M; at 1M, it scores 60.5, compared with 40.0 for the best baseline, Dense + DCA. With our optimized kernels, RecSA is faster than dense attention in end-to-end prefill and decoding from 64K to 2M; at 524K on one H200 GPU, it accelerates prefill by 3.2x and decoding by 3.8x.
candidates.reason: KVキャッシュを木構造で要約し各段で最大k候補だけを選ぶRecSAにより、選択コストと読み取り量を対数オーダーに抑えつつ100万トークン級文脈へ外挿する再帰型スパース注意を提案しており、長文脈推論の注意機構への直接貢献である。
